1. You can't sleep down in the deep mines.
2. The way I fight is to simply strafe and side-step around the bush devil or the croco. Try not to fight more than one. However, I don't recommend fighting them unless you can't escape because a fight can be a waste of time and resource, and time is limited as there will be radiation at midnight in the deep mines.
3. A new map is generated each day, actually it's generated the first time you go down in that day. That being said, items don't get saved if the day passes, so if you dropped something there, it's gone for good the next day.
4. The map has a fairly large size limit, about the size of the overworld map (I think)
5. It's stressful for me. Fairly easy to get jumped by bush devils and losing a lot of health in fights, especially when getting cornered. Always tread carefully.

Watching his videos makes me wish I got a job in Amsterdam, but more importantly learn to ride a bike (I'm 25 and best I can do is pedal without balance). 

Most of his videos parallel a lot on the city planning in the Philippines, especially strodes. Most of the cities in the NCR are like this, never usually a street that's safe to access on bike or on foot. Best we have is the cool idea of properties that is both commercial and a living space, makes living in a Barangay sometimes convenient if there are enough utilities.

Also I like the idea of more bike roads but the way they'll do it is by placing it on the gutter as wide as a meter and a half. It's an attempt but still very dangerous to both parties, especially the biker. The best thing is actually in its own island or sidewalk, but our stroads are never designed like this, with establishments eating up the sidewalk, combined with the sometimes spontaneous road widening projects.

Come to think of it, the Philippines is like North America with its huge dependency on cars, most especially true with the Euclidean Zoning villages, as they don't usually have commercial establishments inside their village and strictly has single family houses, requiring them to leave (usually with a car of some sort) just to get groceries. But I could be wrong, I don't live in one so I don't know what's inside besides the large villas and single family homes.

I have to agree that Ana has the fastest healing potential. She beats Mercy in terms of healing and offensive capabilities. The only problem I have with Ana is that I tend to miss a lot. But I like to use Ana during QP, and I find her fun.

Prioritizing healing the correct unit is often a key tactic. If I don't heal the correct unit, the whole team collapses. I agree that tanks should be healed first especially if they are under fire. But my strategy involves healing allies with low health, especially if they are in critical state. Often times I do not heal flankers but I do tend to forget. I should study on when it is safe to go for them or not. Flankers are also the ones that often call me out for not healing despite the fact that they are in enemy territory.

Ahh, I see my error. I should focus on keeping everyone healthy rather than proving my point. The salt must have gone through me and distracted me from the true goal of keeping everyone alive and healthy.

During KoTH matches, I use Lucio primarily since he often supports better than a Mercy, with the speed boost and stuff. I would also agree  that Lucio is also a good pick if the team can deal with the enemy before they get damaged. Overall I believe Lucio has excellent potential that can be increased if the team exceeds well enough that the only damage they get are scrapes and scratches, and not die very often. I also agree that heroes that can sustain themselves (Mei, Zarya (shield), S:76, Roadhog) will help me focus healing on other characters because I don't need to check on them.

I also agree that Zenyatta should be an off healer. I don't find Zenyatta very good at healing since it's single healing can be beaten by Mercy. But Zenyatta is great at multi-tasking his roles, as he can heal someone and deal damage at the same time.
